name: Wiyot

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Wiyot (wiyo1248).

notes: Skeleton. Algic language (a divergent isolate within Algic, alongside Yurok) of coastal northern California, written in Teeter's Americanist practical orthography (the WikiPron gold this spec is scored against is transcribed with Teeter's letters, not the Wiyot Tribe's alternate orthography). The practical-orthography chart is attributed to Teeter (1964), The Wiyot Language, but that edition's archive.org and HathiTrust copies are lending-restricted with no readable text, so the chart as used here is as reproduced in the Wikipedia phonology section, not independently read from the primary edition. Every remapped value is corroborated distributionally: checking each letter against all 151 words of the WikiPron wiy_latn_broad gold (a source independent of Wikipedia) confirms b=[β], d=[ɾ], g=[ɣ] and r=[ɹ] are approximants/flaps rather than the stops or trill a naive Latin-script reading would expect, the low back vowel o=[ɑ] rather than [o], e=[e] rather than [ɛ], and ch is aspirated [tsʰ] while č is [tʃ] (not the other way around) — all hold with 100% consistency in the gold. c=[ts] and the caron letters č=[tʃ]/š=[ʃ] are separate unaspirated/aspirated series from the ts/ch/lh digraphs already in the table; ł is an alternate single-letter spelling of the ɬ already covered by the lh digraph. The acute/grave accents on vowels are Wiyot's pitch-accent marks (Teeter's culminative-syllable tone), carried through verbatim into the IPA field of the gold transcriptions, so they are mapped as accented vowel symbols rather than stripped. Predictable stress placement and the h~[ʔ] non-word-initial allophony are left unencoded, raising the PER floor: 61 of 151 gold words contain a non-word-initial ⟨h⟩, of which 49 are a standalone h subject to the allophony (the remaining 12 are aspiration digraphs already covered by ph/th/kh/kwh/čh).

Both archive.org copies of this edition (wiyotlanguage0037teet, wiyotlanguage0000karl) are lending-restricted with no OCR text or displayable pages, and HathiTrust's copies are search-only; the primary edition could not be independently read, so no page locator is given. The chart is as reproduced in Wikipedia's Wiyot language phonology section, and every value it gives is independently corroborated: cross-checking each remapped letter against all 151 words of the WikiPron wiy_latn_broad gold (a source independent of Wikipedia) shows b, d, g, r, e, ch and č hold with 100% consistency.
